prompt.context: The client is the North American CEO of a global personal and home care products company. He has hired Capgemini Consulting to turn around the North American business from loss to profitability within two years. We've scheduled the final presentation with the board this afternoon, but the project team is stranded at an airport unable to make the presentation. You are asked to step in and make the presentation instead.
prompt.question: How would you approach turning around the North American business from loss to profitability within two years? Walk through your structure, then analyze the exhibits provided, and identify additional considerations for the CEO.

clarifying_info.q: What are the main revenue streams?
What are the main cost drivers?

clarifying_info.a: Competitors include P&G, Unilever, Johnson & Johnson, Avon, The Body Shop, Henkel KGaA, Reckitt-Benckiser, Shiseido, Jafra Cosmetics, Mary Kay, LVMH, L'Oreal, and Estee Lauder, catering to various customer segments

clarifying_info.q: How intense is rivalry in the cosmetics industry?
clarifying_info.a: Rivalry is present across segments; there are trends toward consolidation and diversification of channel strategies

clarifying_info.q: Through what retail channels are products sold?
clarifying_info.a: Channel strategy details are shown in Exhibit 3; competitors use both dedicated and diverse channel strategies

clarifying_info.q: What are the different consumer segments?
clarifying_info.a: Segments include women and men across age groups; women represent the lion's share of consumption across all three regions (Mexico, USA, Canada)
Female Baby Boomers are driving growth; Echo Boomers will play a greater role beyond 2010
Supply chain, channel strategy, financial situation, org structure, and core competencies are all relevant

exhibits.title: 2009-2014 Growth in Personal Care Consumption by Age Group
exhibits.shows: A chart displaying projected growth rates in personal care consumption broken down by age group and gender across Mexico, USA, and Canada for the period 2009-2014
exhibits.data: Growth rates by age group and gender for three regions: Mexico, USA, Canada; Female Baby Boomers show growth of 8.63% (Mexico), 5.31% (USA), 5.98% (Canada); male 55+ group shows stronger growth than other male age groups

exhibits.title: Ranking Major Household Spending Categories by Share of Wallet and Perception of Need
exhibits.shows: A scatter/quadrant chart plotting major household spending categories on two axes: Perception of Need (Luxury to Necessity) on the x-axis and Share of Wallet (Low to High) on the y-axis
exhibits.data: Categories plotted include: Taxes, Housing, Food (high necessity, high share of wallet); Insurance/Pension, Health Care, Clothing (mid-range); Household Operations, Personal Care (lower share of wallet, moderate necessity); Recreation, Education, Donations/Contributions, Tobacco/Alcohol, Household Furnishings & Equipment (varying positions); Canada census data: Household Products = 4.5% share of wallet, Personal Care = 1.7% share of wallet

exhibits.title: Product-Channel Strategy Map
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot mapping companies by number of product categories (y-axis, 0-16) against channel strategy (x-axis, from Dedicated to Diverse); channel strategy legend distinguishes Primarily Retail vs. Primarily Direct Selling; a trend arrow is shown
exhibits.data: Client is plotted with a large number of product categories but a dedicated channel strategy; P&G, Unilever, Johnson & Johnson, L'Oreal, Estee Lauder are in the diverse channel quadrant with many categories; Avon Cosmetics, Jafra Cosmetics, Mary Kay are in the dedicated/direct-selling area with fewer categories; The Body Shop, Henkel KGaA, Reckitt-Benckiser, Shiseido, LVMH occupy various positions; a trend arrow points toward diverse channel strategy

framework: Internal Analysis: Revenue streams (existing vs. new products), Cost drivers (R&D, manufacturing, operations), Supply chain efficiency, Organizational structure and core competencies
Industry Analysis: Competitor landscape and segments, Intensity of rivalry and consolidation trends, Retail channel structure and relative power of retailers
Customer Analysis: Consumer segments and relative sizes (women vs. men, age cohorts), Client's main consumers and market saturation, Trends in consumer tastes and spending patterns

questions.prompt: Question 1: You are given 3 charts. Take a few minutes to assess and digest the information, then share your observations and analysis.
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers all three exhibits: (1) Exhibit 1 — Women dominate personal care consumption across all three regions; Female Baby Boomers are the major growth driver (8.63%/5.31%/5.98% for Mexico/USA/Canada); male 55+ is a secondary growth pocket; Generation Xers underrepresented except in Mexico; Echo Boomers to watch post-2010. (2) Exhibit 2 — Direct co-relationship between share of wallet and perception of need; Personal Care currently sits relatively low on both axes; moving Personal Care up the necessity axis is key to capturing larger share of wallet; Household Products (4.5%) vs Personal Care (1.7%) illustrates the gap. (3) Exhibit 3 — Client has many product categories but a dedicated channel strategy — misaligned vs. peers; companies with diverse product categories (P&G, Unilever, L'Oreal, Estee Lauder) use diverse channel strategies; there is an industry trend toward diversification; client should shift toward a more diverse distribution channel.

questions.prompt: Question 2: What other considerations should you inform the CEO need further analysis?
questions.guidance: Candidates should cover supply chain / operations topics: (1) Make vs. Buy — pros/cons of in-house manufacturing vs. outsourcing, key constraints, competitor actions; (2) Customer perception — impact of country of origin on brand and marketing strategy; (3) Distribution network location — does current design support future growth? What distance span optimizes service and cost? (4) Decision-making process — current vs. ideal Make/Buy decision process, accountability; (5) Scalability — how will distribution centers scale with growth projections, optimal number and range per DC; (6) Costs — differences across suppliers, standardized cost measurement across regions, consistent accounting, duplicate costs, asset utilization impact, total delivered cost; (7) Information infrastructure — enterprise-wide operational indicators (inventory, costs, service levels), real-time accessibility, cross-regional comparability.

recommendation: The client should focus on women who comprise the lion's share of consumption, while not ignoring growth in the 55+ male group; geographic differences within North America (Mexico vs. USA vs. Canada) must be considered in targeting strategy
The client should develop deep knowledge of customer needs, perception, and spending patterns to capture an increased share of wallet, which is critical for driving long-term, sustainable growth

The client is misplaced in terms of its channel strategy; given its large number of product categories, it should move toward a more diverse distribution channel strategy, similar to Estee Lauder and L'Oreal
risks: The market may not continue growing at the same rate as predicted or may enter a period of decline
Threat of substitute products and changing customer trends can make the client's products less 'necessary', eroding share of wallet
next_steps: Invest in customer research to build deep understanding of needs and perception by segment
Increase marketing spend to shift segment focus toward high-growth Female Baby Boomer and emerging Echo Boomer groups
Conduct thorough cost-benefit analysis of diversifying distribution channels; identify quick wins and phased approach to channel expansion
Evaluate Make/Buy decisions for manufacturing and distribution to optimize total delivered cost
